financials_interim.notes: COMPANY (standalone) basis. See GROUP row's notes for the shared explanation of why Company and Group PBT moved in opposite directions this quarter (JV dividend timing vs JV equity-method share).

Kelani Tyres PLC, FYE 31 March. UNUSUAL STRUCTURE: the Company itself has ZERO direct trading revenue (the P&L's own 'Revenue' line is nil in both periods) -- it does not manufacture or sell anything directly. Its entire profit is generated by (a) a 50%-equity-accounted Joint Venture, CEAT Sri Lanka (the actual tyre/tube manufacturer -- 'Share of results of JV Net of Tax'), plus (b) finance income on its own cash/government-securities portfolio, plus (c) an immaterial wholly-owned subsidiary that hires out motor vehicles (not separately disclosed as material). Given this, `revenue` is left BLANK for both GROUP and COMPANY rows (there is a small 'Operating income' line of Rs.15,732k Group / Rs.15,732k Company for the quarter that is NOT trading revenue -- appears to be a residual/other-income item, not comparable to a normal company's revenue, so not stored as revenue to avoid a misleading cross-company comparison). `operating_profit` = the Company/Group's own reported 'Operating profit' subtotal (a persistent small LOSS at this level: -22,474 Group / -22,464 Company for Q1 FY2026/27), BEFORE Net Finance Income and the JV equity share -- this reflects the holding company's own admin/management overhead against its tiny non-JV income, not a real operating business. Source: documents.source_id '52393' (already registered by the automated collector on 2026-08-12, reused directly -- 'Interim Financial Statements for the Quarter ended 30th June 2026'). unit_scale='000' (Rs'000, explicitly labelled). This entry uses the filing's QUARTER-ONLY figures ('Three Months Ended 30 June 2026') since Kelani Tyres reports discrete quarters, not H1 cumulative, and this is a March-FYE company's first quarter of FY2026/27, period_label = 'Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026)'. Both GROUP and COMPANY bases entered -- these diverge sharply this quarter because the JV's equity-method profit share (162,973k Group PBT contribution) flows only into the consolidated Group result, not the standalone Company result, which instead depends on actual CASH DIVIDENDS received from the JV -- and no dividend was received from the JV in Q1 FY2026/27 (vs a lumpy Rs.750,000k dividend received in Q1 FY2025/26, the prior-year comparative quarter), explaining why Company PBT swung from +750,239k (2025, dividend-inflated) to -4,095k (2026, no dividend this quarter) even as Group PBT swung from -53,467k to +158,868k in the OPPOSITE direction (JV-equity-inflated). finance_costs/finance_income left as separate disclosed lines within operating_profit's build-up but not separately stored (Net Finance Income 18,370k Group / 18,370k Company is already embedded in the path from operating_profit to PBT). current_assets/current_liabilities/inventory/trade_receivables/trade_payables intentionally left BLANK -- this filing does not present a current/non-current split with a conventional trading inventory or trade receivables/payables structure typical of an operating manufacturer (it has 'Trade and other receivables' of only Rs.11,052k, immaterial and not a genuine trade-receivables base given zero revenue -- excluded to avoid implying a trading relationship that does not exist). short_term_borrowings = 'Bank Overdraft' (7,971k, same for both bases). long_term_borrowings left BLANK -- no debt securities or other borrowings line disclosed; 'Retirement benefit obligations' and 'Deferred tax liability' are non-current liabilities but not debt. total_equity, shares_in_issue (80,400,000, per Note 4 Stated Capital) cross-checked exactly against disclosed Net Asset Value per share: Group 7,678,213k/80,400,000=Rs.95.50 (matches exactly); Company 2,107,562k/80,400,000=Rs.26.21 (matches exactly). capex = Purchase of PP&E (65k, same both bases, positive magnitude per project convention).

interim_updates.note_text: Kelani Tyres PLC has no direct trading revenue of its own -- its result is almost entirely a function of its 50% equity-accounted Joint Venture, CEAT Sri Lanka, the actual tyre/tube manufacturer. Group PBT swung to a profit of Rs.158,868k in Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026) from a loss of Rs.53,467k a year earlier, entirely because 'Share of results of JV Net of Tax' swung to +Rs.162,973k from -Rs.53,699k -- a Rs.216,672k swing that is larger than the entire PBT change (Rs.212,335k), meaning Kelani Tyres' own standalone operations (which posted a persistent Rs.22,474k operating loss this quarter, slightly wider than the Rs.16,855k loss a year earlier) actually detracted marginally from the improvement. The JV's own disclosed results (Note, Joint Venture Performance) show why: CEAT Sri Lanka's Profit Before Tax rose 110% to Rs.463,185k (from Rs.220,827k) on Production volume +17.4% (3,082MT to 3,619MT) and Gross Profit +23.0% (Rs.782,063k to Rs.962,539k, driven by Domestic Sales +6.7% to Rs.3,940,711k), but the more dramatic swing is in the JV's own tax line: its tax charge FELL 58.2% to Rs.137,240k (from Rs.328,226k) even as PBT rose, because the prior-year quarter's tax charge (Rs.328,226k) was unusually large relative to that quarter's PBT (Rs.220,827k) -- an effective tax rate of 148.6% in Q1 FY2025/26 versus 29.6% in Q1 FY2026/27 -- which alone flipped the JV from a net LOSS of Rs.107,399k a year ago to a net PROFIT of Rs.325,945k this quarter. At the standalone Company level (excluding JV equity-method consolidation), the picture is the opposite: Company PBT fell to a small loss of Rs.4,095k in Q1 FY2026/27 from a large profit of Rs.750,239k a year earlier, because the Company received a lumpy Rs.750,000k CASH DIVIDEND from the JV in Q1 FY2025/26 (recorded as 'Operating income' at Company level that quarter) that was not repeated in Q1 FY2026/27 -- dividend timing, not any operational change, drives this divergence.

This entry uses the filing's QUARTER-ONLY figures (three months ended 30 June 2026), consistent with how this company reports (discrete quarters, not H1 cumulative, unlike the Dec-FYE banks entered elsewhere this session). `revenue` is deliberately left blank for both bases since the Company genuinely has none -- see the notes field on the GROUP financial_statements row for the full explanation of this company's unusual JV-holding-vehicle structure.
interim_updates.takeaway: This is not a tyre-manufacturing company in its own right -- it is effectively a holding vehicle for a 50% stake in CEAT Sri Lanka. The headline Group profit swing (loss to Rs.159mn profit) is driven roughly 60% by a genuine JV volume/margin improvement (Gross Profit +23% on +17.4% production) and the rest by an unusually large prior-year tax charge at the JV normalizing -- both real, but the second is a comparative-base effect, not a repeatable growth driver. Anyone valuing this stock is really valuing a claim on CEAT Sri Lanka's JV earnings and dividend policy, not Kelani Tyres' own (persistently loss-making) standalone operations.
operational_highlights: Group PBT swung to +Rs.158,868k from -Rs.53,467k YoY, entirely driven by the JV equity-method share swinging to +Rs.162,973k from -Rs.53,699k (a Rs.216,672k swing, larger than the total PBT change)

The JV (CEAT Sri Lanka) itself: PBT +110% to Rs.463,185k on Production +17.4% (3,082MT to 3,619MT) and Gross Profit +23.0% to Rs.962,539k; but its tax charge FELL 58.2% to Rs.137,240k despite higher PBT (effective tax rate 148.6% a year ago vs 29.6% now), which alone flipped the JV from a net loss to a net profit

Company (standalone) PBT fell to -Rs.4,095k from +Rs.750,239k YoY purely because a Rs.750,000k cash dividend received from the JV in Q1 FY2025/26 was not repeated this quarter -- a dividend-timing effect, not an operational change
Kelani Tyres' own standalone operating loss widened slightly to Rs.22,474k (Group) from Rs.16,855k, a persistent small drag funded by finance income on its own cash/government-securities holdings

NAV per share: Rs.95.50 (Group), Rs.26.21 (Company standalone) -- the Rs.69+ gap per share is entirely the market value of Kelani Tyres' 50% JV stake, not reflected in the Company's own standalone balance sheet
key_drivers: JV equity-method share swing (-Rs.53,699k to +Rs.162,973k) is the single dominant driver of the Group result, itself split between a genuine volume/margin improvement at CEAT Sri Lanka and an unusually high prior-year comparative tax charge normalizing
CEAT Sri Lanka's effective tax rate fell to 29.6% from 148.6% YoY -- this alone explains why the JV swung from a net loss to a net profit even though its own PBT growth (+110%) was already strong
No JV dividend was declared/received in Q1 FY2026/27 versus a Rs.750,000k dividend in Q1 FY2025/26 -- explains the Company-standalone PBT swing in the OPPOSITE direction to the Group result
